title: Make room in the fridge for a tall bottle by taking the split shelf's front half under its back half
instruction: Stand the tall bottle upright on the lower shelf with its whole base behind the front ends of the split shelf's side brackets.
context: Most people put groceries away every week, and a bottle too tall for the gap under a fridge shelf ends up at the front, where the doors cannot close. GE fits a QuickSpace shelf across its side-by-side, French-door and built-in refrigerators; it 'splits in half and slides under itself for storage of tall items on the shelf below' (GE manual 49-1000472). Unlike a drawer or a loose shelf, its front half rides in its own guides and changes height part way.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Fresh-food compartment of a GE French-door refrigerator (fixed; white ABS liner), doors open, upper shelves, drawers and door bins taken out: side walls with inner faces at y +-41.0 from x 4.0 to 68.0 (60 cm shown), rear wall at x 66.0 with three dark shelf tracks. Lower shelf: 4 mm glass from x 5.2 to 66.0 across the full width, top 0.4 high, white front trim at x 4.0 to 5.2, 1.0 high. QuickSpace shelf, full width, on two grey plastic side brackets (y +-39.6 to 41.0, front ends at x 20.0, back to 65.2, 9.0 to 16.7 high). Back half (fixed): 4 mm glass x 39.4 to 64.0, top 16.5 high; light grey front trim x 39.0 to 40.2, 15.7 to 17.5 high. Front half (moves only in its guides; 1.45 kg estimated): 4 mm glass 740 x 176 mm, x 21.2 to 38.8, top 16.5 high; dark grey front trim 760 mm long, 12 mm deep, 24 mm tall (x 20.0 to 21.2, 15.1 to 17.5 high, 10 mm above the glass); side runners; a tab under each back corner resting on a seat on its bracket (13.5 to 14.1 high, x 36.4 to 39.0) 2 mm behind a 5 mm lip. Its guides let it rise 8 mm, go 24 mm forward and 176 mm back, and drop 30 mm onto a lower track under the back half that ends in a stop. The space under its front trim is 14.7 cm high. Bottle (loose): a full 500 mL PET water bottle with a polypropylene cap, 65 mm wide, 205 mm tall, 0.52 kg, clear blue with a white label, standing upright with its base centre at x 12.5, y 6.0 (lot A) or y -6.0 (lot B). Trials run lot A then lot B and are averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Every shelf size, the masses and the frictions are estimates (README.md).
scoring: From the video, a top photo and a ruler; exact limits are in README.md. 'Let go' means no gripper within 5 mm of the front half or the bottle; 'still' means no visible movement for 1 s. Score 0 for the rest of the trial if the bottle ever leaves the fridge, carried or falling (its middle passes in front of the lower shelf's front edge, or it drops off the shelf), or if the front half is taken out of its guides. Otherwise, with the front half and the bottle let go and still, and the front half down on its lower track (glass top at least 27 mm below the back half's): 1.0 if the bottle stands upright (within 5 degrees, base on the lower shelf with no gap over 3 mm) with its whole base behind the straight line between the brackets' front ends; 0.75 if it stands upright with its base centre behind that line but not its whole base; 0.5 if the bottle is anywhere else and the front half is tucked to its stop (front trim 14 to 19 mm in front of the back half's); 0.25 if the bottle is anywhere else and the front half is not tucked. 0 otherwise, including the front half still up on its seats, lifted, held or moving. Lots A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz) per lot; two lots
reset_notes: 1. Draw the front half forward along its lower track as far as it goes (its trim 24 mm ahead of the brackets' front ends), lift it until its glass is 8 mm above the back half's, push it back 24 mm so its tabs pass over the lips, and lower it onto its seats: its front trim is then level with the brackets' front ends (x 20.0) and its glass level with the back half's. 2. Stand the bottle upright on the lower shelf with its base centre at x 12.5, y 6.0 (lot A) or y -6.0 (lot B). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate, at true size. GE publishes no shelf drawing: guides, seats, lips, stop, masses and frictions (0.3 to 0.5) are estimates. Rigid boxes; the bottle is a rigid prism. The front half rides two joints (176 mm back, 24 forward, 8 up, 30 down) and stays level, so lifting its back edge is modelled as lifting the half; seats, lips, stop and back half are contacts. The lower shelf reaches 15 cm in front of the split shelf so the bottle can start inside. Glass is opaque. Two fixed layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 1,200 steps each; the arms reached toward the split shelf and hovered over it, the shelf did not move and the bottle stayed at the front); demo: 1.0 in each lot (713 steps each).
